y-m-29-08.title: How many points can a line and parabola share?
y-m-29-08.topic: Quadratic graphs and lines: number of intersections based on k
y-m-29-08.goal: Test “works in few examples, so always” around where value changes; make examples with exactly 2 intersections, explain using minimum why 1 or none.
y-m-29-08.material:
Draw parabola y=x² and line y=2x+k on same coordinates. k decide y-coordinate where line meet y-axis. (Read y=2x+k as “y equals two x plus k”; x²−2x read “x squared minus two x”.) Intersection x values solve x²=2x+k, that is x²−2x=k. Table below gives x²−2x. Read horizontally.
x | −2 | −1 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
x²−2x | 8 | 3 | 0 | −1 | 0 | 3 | 8

y-m-29-08.s.s1.r.a: Testing good, but no standard for which values. First find where table values change.
y-m-29-08.s.s1.o.b: Test k around where table values go down then back up, −1 or −2.
y-m-29-08.s.s1.r.b: You use clue that minimum in table where intersection count may change.
y-m-29-08.s.s1.o.c: Both examples gave 2, enough; accept Minjun idea
y-m-29-08.s.s1.r.c: You claim “any number” from few examples. Other k types may be untested.
y-m-29-08.s.s1.o.d: Test more k bigger than table, like 8,15,24 [15 8]
y-m-29-08.s.s1.r.d: You only add more large values. Look how x²−2x change in table.
y-m-29-08.s.s1.explain: More same-type examples no counterexample. Intersection number may change near minimum x²−2x (−1 at x=1). Testing k near that, like −1 or −2, meaningful. Last step explain why.
y-m-29-08.s.s2.prompt: Find 3 different k where line/parabola meet at exactly 2 points and both intersection x coordinates integers. Enter k and x₁,x₂ (integers from −9 to 9).

y-m-29-08.s.s2.fail.c2: If x₁=x₂, only one intersection. Write 2 different k values.
y-m-29-08.s.s2.fail.c3: x₁ or x₂ no satisfy x²=2x+k. Substitute and compare both sides.
y-m-29-08.s.s2.explain: Rows with repeated value: 0 at x=0,2; 3 at x=−1,3; 8 at x=−2,4. Also any integer pair x₁+x₂=2 works (e.g. x=−3,5 gives k=15); both intersection points same distance left and right of x=1. Swapping x₁,x₂ same k, so same example. [0 1 2 2 3 3 4 5]
y-m-29-08.s.s3.prompt: When k=−1 only 1 intersection; when k=−2 none. Explain using table or expression.

y-m-29-08.s.s3.model.0: Minimum x²−2x na −1 at x=1. If k=−1, only x=1 works, one point. k=−2 smaller, so no intersection.
y-m-29-08.s.s3.model.1: Table x²−2x never go below −1. k=−1 only x=1 works; k=−2 no x works, so no meeting.
y-m-29-08.s.s3.model.2: x²−2x=(x−1)²−1, so no smaller than −1. k=−1 meets only at x=1; k=−2 no solution.

y-m-29-01.title: Which plan suit my younger sibling?
y-m-29-01.topic: Use linear functions: compare two plans and boundary usage
y-m-29-01.goal: Represent two quantities growing at steady rate, like charges, with linear functions. Learn which cheaper can depend on usage; change judgment and confidence as new information come; design a new plan meeting conditions.
y-m-29-01.material:
My younger sibling wan choose mobile data plan. If monthly use x GB (number at least 0; decimals okay), monthly cost y (원) for both plans below.
Plan A: basic fee 3000원 + 500원 per 1 GB, that is y=500x+3000
Plan B: basic fee 6000원 + 300원 per 1 GB, that is y=300x+6000
(Read y=500x+3000 as “y equals five hundred x plus three thousand”. Assume per-GB charge no change even for big use. Amounts are made up.) The rate is per 1GB.

y-m-29-02.title: Line wey rise faster always stay on top?

y-m-29-03.title: Which way graph of (x−2)² move?
y-m-29-03.topic: Quadratic graphs: direction of shift in y=a(x−p)²+q
y-m-29-03.goal: Check if direction guessed only from expression shape match table values; use matching equal-value places to determine shift, and apply to new expression.
y-m-29-03.material:
Haeun talk about how graph y=(x−2)² move from y=x²: “Expression subtract 2 from x, so x decrease by 2. Haeun put x values in to make y table. Read horizontally.
x | −2 | −1 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
y=x² | 4 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 4 | 9 | 16
y=(x−2)² | 16 | 9 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 4

y-m-29-03.s.s1.explain: In y=x², value 0 at x=0, 1 at x=±1, and 4 at x=±2. In y=(x−2)², 0 at x=2, 1 at x=1 and 3, 4 at x=0 and 4. All move 2 to right, where x larger. Haeun direction no match table. x must be 2 bigger to get same y.

y-m-29-04.title: Vegetable garden by wall: which shape get biggest area?
y-m-29-04.topic: Use quadratic functions: biggest area for rectangle beside wall
y-m-29-04.goal: Check if earlier rule (same perimeter, square get biggest area) still apply under new condition; make different designs meeting conditions and explain why area grow then shrink.
y-m-29-04.material: You want make rectangular vegetable garden by a wall using 20m wire fence. Wall side need no fence, fence cover other 3 sides only. Use all fence, nothing left. y-m-29-04.prereq.0: Rectangle area, multiplication of natural numbers (elementary to Grade 7) [1]

y-m-29-05.goal: Think how far linear function from two records be valid; decide what else to check before trusting prediction, explain why expression value and real-life value fit differ.
y-m-29-05.material: Water enter empty rectangular tank through hose. Start time na 0 minutes and water level (height from bottom to surface) na 0cm. Record: 12cm at 3 minutes and 20cm at 5 minutes. y-m-29-06.title: How width of parabola change when a change?
y-m-29-06.topic: Quadratic y=ax²: how a sign and size affect graph
y-m-29-06.goal: Use table values step by step to judge how size/sign of a in y=ax² affect width/opening direction; find counterexample and rewrite rule.
y-m-29-06.material: Sua compare graphs (parabolas) y=ax² like y=x² and y=2x². (Read y=ax² as “y equals a x squared”; a nonzero.) Parabola width mean left-right distance at same height size (absolute y). Sua think, “Bigger a, narrower width.” Check with tables one by one if right. [0]
